climate.overview_html: COP31 opens in Antalya in four days. Pre-sessional technical negotiations commenced November 5, with the main high-level session opening November 9; climate finance, fossil fuel phase-out language and adaptation remain the central battle lines. Brazil published a voluntary global fossil fuel phase-out roadmap—framed as a bridge proposal, not a negotiating text—positioning itself between major oil producers and climate-vulnerable nations. The Pacific Pre-COP Taku Pakasoa Declaration backs faster emissions cuts and accessible direct finance for small island states. WMO’s October ocean update projects the 2026 El Niño Niño 3.4 anomaly peaking near +3.7°C—the strongest El Niño ever recorded by this metric and over 1°C above the previous 2015–16 record. The official Copernicus C3S October 2026 monthly bulletin—expected to confirm October as the warmest on record at ~1.76°C above preindustrial—remained unpublished as of November 5.

items.headline: COP31 Pre-Sessional Negotiations Open in Antalya; Main Session Opens November 9; Finance, Fossil Fuels and Adaptation Are Key Battle Lines
items.summary: Technical pre-sessional negotiations for COP31 opened in Antalya, Turkey on November 5, with the main high-level conference commencing November 9. The core battle lines heading into negotiations are: agreeing a New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG) on climate finance as a credible successor to the failed $100 billion-per-year pledge; language on fossil fuel phase-out following the UAE COP28 breakthrough; and whether adaptation finance receives a dedicated agenda item. Developed-country delegations emphasise the NCQG; developing nations and small island states prioritise adaptation and loss and damage operationalisation.

items.headline: Brazil Presents Voluntary Global Fossil Fuel Phase-Out Roadmap Ahead of COP31; Officials Stress It Is Not a Negotiating Text
items.summary: Brazil's government published a voluntary roadmap for a managed global fossil fuel phase-out ahead of COP31, framing it as a bridge proposal rather than a formal negotiating text. Brazilian officials stressed the plan accommodates different national energy security circumstances and transition timelines. The move positions Brazil — simultaneously a major oil exporter and one of the world's largest clean energy producers — as a potential dealmaker between major fossil fuel producers and climate-vulnerable nations at Antalya. The roadmap calls for a managed exit rather than an abrupt phase-out, echoing language from the UAE COP28 'transition away' compromise.

items.headline: Pacific Pre-COP Concludes with Taku Pakasoa Declaration: Faster Emissions Cuts, Accessible Climate Finance, Ocean Protection
items.summary: The Pacific Pre-COP, with government meetings in Fiji and a leaders' retreat in Tuvalu, concluded with the Taku Pakasoa Declaration. Pacific leaders — among the most climate-vulnerable nations — called for accelerated emissions reductions consistent with 1.5°C, more accessible and direct climate finance for small island developing states, and strengthened protection of oceans as a global climate regulator. The declaration aligned with the COP31 Presidency's agenda of launching electrification pledges and adding ocean protection to the summit programme on Energy Day, November 10.

items.headline: WMO: 2026 El Niño Niño 3.4 Projected to Peak Near +3.7°C in December—Strongest Ever Recorded; Previous Record +2.6°C (2015–16)
items.summary: WMO's October ocean temperature update confirms the 2026 El Niño is the strongest on record by several metrics. The Niño 3.4 index anomaly is projected to peak near +3.7°C in October–December 2026, surpassing the previous record of +2.6°C set in November 2015–January 2016 by over 1°C. The event is driving record global surface temperatures, the exceptional 2026 Atlantic and Pacific tropical cyclone seasons, the Bay of Bengal back-to-back cyclone sequence, the prolonged Southeast Asian peatland fire crisis, and the 13 consecutive months above 1.5°C. WMO warns that peak impacts on regional precipitation patterns may not arrive until 2027 during the La Niña transition.

items.headline: October 2026 Projected Warmest October on Record at ~1.76°C Above Preindustrial; 13th Consecutive Month Above 1.5°C; Official C3S Bulletin Pending
items.summary: October 2026 closed as the projected warmest October in the ERA5 instrumental record at approximately 1.76°C above preindustrial averages, driven by the record 2026 El Niño. The result marks the 13th consecutive month with global temperatures above the 1.5°C Paris threshold. The official Copernicus C3S monthly climate bulletin for October had not been published as of November 5.

items.headline: NDC Synthesis Report: Full Implementation of All Current NDCs Still Leads to 2.3–2.5°C Warming by 2100—~1°C Above the Paris Limit
items.summary: A Böll Foundation analysis of the UNFCCC NDC Synthesis Report finds that even full implementation of every NDC submitted ahead of COP31 would still result in 2.3–2.5°C above preindustrial levels by 2100 — roughly 1°C above the Paris 1.5°C limit. The analysis stresses that the absence of credible climate finance commitments directly undermines developing countries' ability to submit more ambitious NDCs.

items.headline: EU Climate Chief Hoekstra: COP31 Finance Talks ‘Dead in the Water’; Mobilised Climate Finance at $136.7 Billion vs. $300 Billion Goal
items.summary: EU Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra told Bloomberg that talks on new climate finance commitments at COP31 are 'dead in the water,' arguing major new pledges must come from outside the EU. Developed-country mobilised climate finance reached $136.7 billion in 2025 against a $300 billion-per-year 2035 goal. The Pilot Resilience Fund — meant to raise $500 million by COP31 — has secured only $180 million in pledges.

major_events.name: Florida Extreme Flooding — St. Johns Nearing Major Flood Stage; Emergency Expanded to 14 Counties; Two Deaths Confirmed
major_events.status: Escalating river flooding — St. Johns River near Astor is approaching major flood stage and expected to crest at or above 25 ft by late weekend; Governor’s emergency declaration expanded to 14 counties including Lake, Seminole and Volusia; Brevard County schools closed third consecutive day; two deaths confirmed statewide
major_events.impact: Following the November 2 extreme rainfall event (up to 15 inches in Brevard County), rivers across east and west-central Florida remain elevated and are still rising in some areas. The transition from flash flood emergency to slow-drain river flooding means the event's duration is extending into next week. The simultaneous November 2 king-tide surge and the sustained river flooding compound infrastructure stress along the northeast Florida coastline.

major_events.name: Southwest US Flooding Aftermath — One Confirmed Death in Flagstaff; Cleanup Expected to Take Weeks; Four States Affected
major_events.status: Recovery — extreme atmospheric river event from November 1–2 has ended; one death confirmed in Flagstaff, Arizona; infrastructure damage spans Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico and portions of Nevada; active cleanup underway across Flagstaff, Sedona, Tucson, Durango and Pagosa Springs; more than 10 all-time flood gauge records broken across three states; cleanup expected to take several weeks
major_events.impact: The Four Corners atmospheric river produced historic flooding across the Southwest. Separately, 19 inches fell in six hours near the Louisiana border in southwest Mississippi — a simultaneous extreme event pointing to an exceptional large-scale moisture pattern. Attribution research is expected to examine the role of the record 2026 El Niño-elevated SSTs in amplifying atmospheric moisture flux.

major_events.name: Southeast Asian Peatland Haze (Indonesia / Borneo / Sumatra) — Ongoing; ~40 Million Exposed; Wet Season Transition Underway
major_events.status: Ongoing, slow easing — wet season onset beginning in some areas of Sumatra and Kalimantan is reducing surface fire intensity, but underground peat fires at depths up to 8 m continue and are extremely difficult to extinguish; bilateral Indonesia–Singapore task force remains operational; more than 333,470 acute respiratory cases across seven Indonesian provinces recorded
major_events.impact: ~40 million people region-wide continue to experience elevated PM2.5. The El Niño peak in December threatens to further delay the wet-season transition in the most fire-prone peatland areas, potentially extending the haze crisis into late November. The fires have produced an estimated CO₂ release that will register as a measurable atmospheric spike in November–December ERA5 data.

weather.overview_html: Florida’s flooding crisis is escalating: the St. Johns River near Astor is now approaching major flood stage, the Governor’s emergency declaration has expanded to 14 counties, two deaths have been confirmed, and Brevard County schools have been closed for a third consecutive day. In the Southwest, one death has been confirmed in Flagstaff, Arizona from the November 1–2 atmospheric river; cleanup is expected to take weeks. In the central Pacific, NHC assigns a 70% development probability to a tropical disturbance within five days—no land threat expected at this range. The Southeast Asian peatland haze continues with ~40 million exposed.

items.headline: St. Johns River Near Astor Nearing Major Flood Stage; Expected to Crest at or Above 25 ft by Late Weekend; Active Flood Warnings Extend Through Next Week
items.summary: The St. Johns River near Astor in Volusia and Lake counties is approaching major flood stage (25 ft threshold) as continuous upstream inflow from the November 2 extreme rainfall event fills the river system. NWS Melbourne has extended active flood warnings. The river is projected to crest at or above major flood stage by the late weekend, with elevated levels expected for days after cresting. The transition from flash flood emergency to slow-drain river flooding means the event's duration is extending into next week.

items.headline: Florida Flooding: Governor’s Emergency Declaration Expands to 14 Counties; Lake, Seminole and Volusia Added; Two Deaths Confirmed
items.summary: Florida's Governor expanded the state of emergency declaration for the ongoing flooding event to 14 counties as river flooding spread north from Brevard County. Lake, Seminole and Volusia counties were added to the declaration following NWS flood warnings as the St. Johns River rose toward major flood stage. Two deaths have been confirmed statewide due to the flooding event, which began with the November 2 extreme rainfall.

items.headline: Brevard County Schools Remain Closed Third Consecutive Day; Active Flood Warnings and Road Closures Persist
items.summary: Brevard County schools remained closed for a third consecutive day on November 5, with the district citing active flood warnings and ongoing road closures affecting student and staff safety. The St. Johns River and its tributaries remain at or near flood stage across the county following the November 2 historic rainfall that produced up to 15 inches in some locations.

items.headline: Southwest US Flooding: One Death Confirmed in Flagstaff; Damage Spans Four States; Cleanup Expected to Take Weeks
items.summary: One death has been confirmed in Flagstaff, Arizona, following the November 1–2 Four Corners atmospheric river event. Infrastructure damage spans Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico and portions of Nevada, with road closures, bridge damage and utility disruptions across multiple communities including Flagstaff, Sedona, Tucson, Durango and Pagosa Springs. Cleanup operations are expected to take several weeks; full damage assessment is ongoing. Attribution research on the role of El Niño-elevated SSTs in amplifying the event is under way.

items.headline: NHC Central Pacific Disturbance at 70% Five-Day Development Probability; Warm SSTs and Low Shear Favour Organisation; No Land Threat at This Range
items.summary: The National Hurricane Center's Global Tropical Weather Outlook assigns a 70% probability of tropical cyclone development within five days to a disturbance in the central Pacific as of November 5. The system is embedded in a favourable environment of low wind shear and anomalously warm sea surface temperatures linked to the record-intensity 2026 El Niño. No impact to land areas is forecast within the five-day outlook window; NHC will monitor the system's organisation.

items.headline: Southeast Asian Peatland Haze: Indonesia–Singapore Task Force Active; ~40 Million Exposed; Underground Peat Fires at 8 m Depth Continuing Even as Wet Season Begins
items.summary: The 2026 Southeast Asian peatland haze crisis continues. Underground peat fires at depths up to 8 metres resist wet-season rain onset across Sumatra and Kalimantan. ~40 million people exposed to elevated PM2.5 across Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore. 333,470+ acute respiratory cases across seven Indonesian provinces. The Indonesia–Singapore bilateral task force remains operational. The El Niño peak in December threatens to extend the crisis into late November.

renewables.overview_html: Array Technologies and Shoals Technologies announced an all-stock merger, combining tracker systems with electrical balance-of-system products to create an integrated solar infrastructure platform. Tata Power Renewable commissioned its 300 MW SECI project in Koppal, Karnataka, pushing its total renewable portfolio to 12 GW. India’s NHPC and Essar Renewables announced a $475 million hybrid solar, wind and BESS partnership in Andhra Pradesh. At the ongoing Bharat Renewable Energy Summit 2026, officials confirmed India’s non-fossil electricity capacity has surpassed 310 GW, meeting its Paris target five years early.

items.headline: Array Technologies and Shoals Technologies Agree All-Stock Merger; Creates Integrated Solar Infrastructure Platform Spanning Trackers and Electrical BOS
items.summary: Array Technologies (solar tracker systems) and Shoals Technologies (electrical balance of systems, connectors and BOS products) announced an all-stock merger agreement, creating an integrated solar infrastructure platform. The combined company will offer bundled procurement and single-vendor service for large-scale solar projects, targeting improved cost efficiencies for utility-scale developers. The deal is subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.

items.headline: Tata Power Renewable Commissions 300 MW SECI Solar Project in Koppal, Karnataka; Total Renewable Portfolio Reaches 12 GW
items.summary: Tata Power Renewable Energy commissioned its 300 MW SECI-awarded solar project at Koppal, Karnataka, bringing the company's total renewable energy portfolio to 12 GW — a milestone marking a 20x growth in its renewable capacity over the past decade. The Koppal project is one of the largest single-site solar installations commissioned in Karnataka and directly supports India's national renewable energy targets.

items.headline: India’s Installed Wind Power Capacity Reaches 59.2 GW as of September 2026; 11% Year-on-Year Growth; Government Targets 8 GW New Installations in FY27
items.summary: India's total installed wind power capacity reached 59.2 GW as of September 2026, representing 11% year-on-year growth, per Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) data. The government is targeting 8 GW of new wind capacity additions in FY 2026-27 as part of the broader push to 500 GW of non-fossil energy capacity by 2030–2031 announced at the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit.

items.headline: NHPC and Essar Renewables to Partner on $475 Million Hybrid Renewable Energy Project in Andhra Pradesh; Solar, Wind and Battery Storage
items.summary: India's National Hydroelectric Power Corporation (NHPC) and Essar Renewables announced a partnership to develop a $475 million hybrid renewable energy project in Andhra Pradesh, integrating solar PV, wind and battery energy storage systems to supply renewable power. The deal builds on existing collaboration between the two companies in state-awarded RE tenders and aligns with Andhra Pradesh's aggressive renewable energy expansion targets.

items.headline: Squadron Energy Receives State Planning Approval for 420 MW Moreton Hill Wind Farm in Victoria, Australia; Up to 62 Turbines
items.summary: Squadron Energy, one of Australia's largest renewable energy developers, received state planning approval for its 420 MW Moreton Hill wind farm in Victoria, which will incorporate up to 62 wind turbines. The approval is a key development milestone for the project, contributing to Australia's target of 82% renewable electricity by 2030.

items.headline: PM Modi Opens Bharat Renewable Energy Summit 2026: India Crosses 310 GW Non-Fossil Capacity, Meets Paris Target 5 Years Early; 500 GW Additional by 2030
items.summary: PM Modi inaugurated the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit 2026 (November 2–5, New Delhi), announcing India has surpassed 310 GW of non-fossil power capacity (>50% of total installed power), meeting its Paris Agreement climate commitment five years ahead of schedule. Solar capacity grew from 2.8 GW to 171 GW; wind from 21 GW to 60 GW. Modi set an additional 500 GW non-fossil capacity target by 2030–2031.

items.headline: Solar Sector Corporate Funding Up 45% Year-on-Year Through Three Quarters of 2026; 88 M&A Transactions in 9M 2026 vs. 76 in 9M 2025
items.summary: Solar sector corporate funding rose 45% year-on-year through the first three quarters of 2026, per PV Magazine analysis. The sector recorded 88 M&A transactions in 9M 2026, up from 76 in 9M 2025. Notable deals included Inox Solar Americas' $750 million purchase of Boviet Solar and Drax's $737 million acquisition of Bluefield Solar Income Fund. Growth reflects sustained data-centre and industrial load demand for clean energy capacity.

items.headline: US Interior Dept Seeks Court Reconsideration of Permits for Four Major Offshore Wind Projects Including 704 MW Revolution Wind and 1.7 GW Maryland Offshore Wind
items.summary: The US Interior and Justice Departments have sought court reconsideration of construction and operations plan approvals for at least four East Coast offshore wind projects: the 704 MW Revolution Wind (partly operational), the 1.7 GW Maryland Offshore Wind project, Atlantic Shores (NJ) and New England Wind (MA). ~300 wind and solar projects also await Department of Defense review.

items.headline: India’s SECI Launches Largest-Yet 4 GW/16 GWh Standalone Battery Storage Tender for Rajasthan and Gujarat; Bid Deadline November 24
items.summary: India's Solar Energy Corporation (SECI) invited bids for 4,000 MW/16,000 MWh of standalone BESS — 2,500 MW/10,000 MWh in Rajasthan and 1,500 MW/6,000 MWh in Gujarat — its largest standalone BESS tender to date. Bid deadline: November 24. Directly supports India's 27,000 MW BESS capacity target by FY2030.

items.headline: Equinor Delays 810 MW Empire Wind First Power to H1 2027 Due to US Shipbuilding Constraints; Total Capex Unchanged
items.summary: Equinor's 810 MW Empire Wind project off New York — approximately 80% complete — will not deliver first power until H1 2027, delayed from a 2026 target, due to US domestic shipbuilding requirements for installation support vessels. Total capex is unchanged; $3 billion+ project financing package is in place.

science.overview_html: Two new preprints this week address core challenges in AI weather forecasting: Sonny-ENS applies score-based diffusion to generate calibrated probabilistic ensembles that outperform IFS-ENS on CRPS at lead times up to 10 days, and a diagnostic framework separates initial-condition error from intrinsic model error in AI weather forecasts—a critical step for principled uncertainty quantification. A GRL study confirms accelerating Arctic warming is weakening the boreal carbon sink. ECMWF’s AIFS-COMPO remains the standout operational milestone of the past week, and FitzRoy continues to represent the leading edge of regional ML forecasting preprints.

items.headline: arXiv:2611.01614 — Sonny-ENS: Score-Based Probabilistic Weather Forecasting Ensemble Outperforming IFS-ENS on CRPS at Lead Times Up to 10 Days
items.summary: Sonny-ENS applies a score-based diffusion approach to global probabilistic weather forecasting, generating ensembles by drawing samples from a learned conditional score function. The preprint reports that Sonny-ENS outperforms IFS-ENS on CRPS skill scores for lead times from 3 to 10 days, while maintaining ensemble spread calibration superior to other diffusion-based weather models. Addresses a key limitation of earlier diffusion weather models that trade ensemble sharpness against spread calibration.

items.headline: arXiv:2611.05592 — Separating Initial-Condition vs. Model Error in AI Weather Forecasts: Attribution Framework for Downstream Probabilistic Skill Degradation
items.summary: This preprint presents a diagnostic framework that disentangles initial-condition (IC) error from intrinsic model error in AI weather forecast degradation — a critical problem as AI models increasingly outperform physics-based counterparts on average metrics while showing unpredictable failure modes at longer leads. The framework attributes probabilistic skill degradation at lead times beyond 5 days to specific IC error sources vs. model uncertainty, enabling more principled uncertainty quantification and informing AI model development priorities.

items.headline: GRL: Accelerating Arctic Warming Now Inhibiting Net Land Carbon Uptake in Northern High Latitudes—Boreal Carbon Sink Weakening Signal
items.meta: Madani et al. · Geophysical Research Letters doi:10.1029/2026GL122135
items.summary: A GRL study finds that progressive warming is inhibiting net land carbon uptake in northern high latitudes, with moisture deficits, heightened soil respiration, and permafrost carbon release outpacing vegetation productivity gains. The findings signal measurable weakening of the Arctic and boreal carbon sink — a major carbon feedback — reinforcing the need to represent permafrost carbon processes in IPCC-class Earth system models and AI climate emulators targeting decadal projections.

items.headline: China CMA Deploys Two Operational AI Weather Systems: Typhoon Cloud-Pattern Recognition and 4-Hour Severe Convective Prediction Using Fengyun Satellite Data
items.summary: China's Meteorological Administration unveiled two new operational AI weather systems: a typhoon cloud-pattern recognition model interpreting storm structure from Fengyun satellite imagery in real time, and a model predicting severe convective weather up to four hours in advance. Both are deployed operationally within the CMA's national forecast suite.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.40641 — Agentic AI Framework Connects Extreme-Weather Probabilistic Forecasts to Agricultural and Adaptation Impact Estimates End-to-End
items.summary: An agentic AI framework couples a weather-event detection module with an agricultural impact model, enabling automated end-to-end assessment from probabilistic forecast output to expected crop, livestock or infrastructure effects in near-real-time — addressing the critical gap between high-impact weather warnings and sector-specific impact projections.

items.headline: GRL: ‘Permafrost Detachment Slides’—Climate-Driven Bottom-Up Failure Mode—Expected to Become More Frequent; 150+ Documented in Mackenzie Valley
items.summary: A GRL study identifies 'permafrost detachment slides' as a distinct bottom-up failure mechanism: slides fail from the base upward due to decades of ~0.3°C/decade permafrost warming combined with historic wildfire disturbance. The Mackenzie Valley alone has more than 150 such slides. Events of this type will become more frequent with continued warming, with implications for Arctic communities and infrastructure.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.38775 — FitzRoy: Reinforcement-Guided Diffusion Model Jointly Optimises Forecast Skill and Physical Realism for Continental US Precipitation
items.summary: FitzRoy applies reinforcement-guided diffusion to precipitation forecasting over the continental US, jointly optimising predictive skill and physical realism via a reinforcement learning reward signal. Standard diffusion-based weather models trade off sharp but physically implausible fields against smooth oversmoothed outputs; FitzRoy's RL guidance drives the diffusion process toward physically consistent outputs while retaining skill. Evaluated against MRMS radar observations and standard probabilistic metrics.

items.headline: ECMWF Introduces AIFS-COMPO: AI System Extends Neural Weather Forecasting to Aerosols and Reactive Gases; 10-Day Global Air Quality Forecasts in 50 Seconds per GPU
items.meta: Alexe et al. (ECMWF) · arXiv:2604.03300 · Experimental operational deployment October 2026
items.summary: ECMWF's experimental AIFS-COMPO system jointly predicts meteorological variables and atmospheric composition — aerosols (AOD, PM2.5) and reactive gases (ozone, NO2). It produces 3-hourly, 10-day global forecasts in 50 seconds on a single GPU, vs. ~1,000 seconds on 8,000 CPUs for operational IFS-COMPO. AIFS-COMPO achieves lower errors than IFS-COMPO for 5-day AOD and PM2.5 forecasts. Remains experimental — not replacing operational CAMS.

items.title: Array Technologies and Shoals Technologies Announce All-Stock Merger; Creates Integrated Solar Infrastructure Platform
items.body_html: Array Technologies and Shoals Technologies announced an all-stock merger agreement on November 4, combining Array’s solar tracker systems with Shoals’ electrical balance-of-system products and wire harness connectors to create an integrated solar infrastructure platform. The combined company is expected to offer bundled procurement and single-vendor service for large-scale utility solar projects, targeting cost efficiencies across the hardware value chain. The deal is subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.

items.title: Two Point O Capital Raises $10 Million Led by Transition Venture Capital to Scale Climate Intelligence Platform
items.body_html: Two Point O Capital raised $10 million in a funding round led by Transition Venture Capital, with participation from climate-focused co-investors. Two Point O provides climate intelligence and data analytics services for financial institutions quantifying physical climate risk in investment portfolios. The raise will be used to scale its data infrastructure and expand coverage from individual asset-level risk scoring to portfolio-level climate-adjusted valuations.

items.title: CESC/Purvah Green Extends ReNew 1.4 GWp Acquisition Deadline to November 21—~$510 M Deal Still Pending
items.body_html: India’s CESC Limited and its renewable arm Purvah Green Power have amended the share purchase agreement for their ~1.4 GWp ReNew Solar Power acquisition, extending the closing deadline 21 days to November 21, 2026. The deal covers six SPVs holding approximately 1.4 GWp of contracted operating solar capacity at an enterprise value of ~₹4,859 crore (~US$510 million), with more than 90% contracted with SECI.

items.title: BW ESS Acquires 200 MW/800 MWh French Battery Storage Portfolio from Recurrent Energy (Canadian Solar)—Enters Seventh Global Market
items.body_html: BW Energy Storage Systems acquired two ready-to-build standalone BESS projects in France from Canadian Solar’s subsidiary Recurrent Energy, comprising a 100 MW/400 MWh project at Baixas (Eastern Pyrénées) and a second 100 MW/400 MWh project at Coquainvilliers (Calvados). The deal marks BW ESS’s entry into France, its seventh market globally, adding to existing positions in the UK, Italy, Germany, Spain, Australia and the US. BW ESS’s CEO described the projects as complementing France’s predominantly nuclear grid with large-scale rapid-response battery flexibility.

items.title: Vaisala Completes Acquisition of AI Weather Company Atmo, Inc.—USD 70 M Fixed + Up to USD 60 M Earn-Out; Deepens AI Forecasting Strategy
items.body_html: Finnish measurement technology leader Vaisala completed the acquisition of AI weather forecasting company Atmo, Inc. on October 29, four months after announcing the deal. The fixed purchase price was USD 70 million, with a contingent earn-out of up to USD 60 million tied to 2026–2028 performance targets. The deal “supports Vaisala’s strategic priority to grow its services and software revenue” alongside its traditional hardware and sensor businesses.
